title: Symplectic Reck: In-Situ Learning of Gaussian Quantum Operations
claim: A triangular mesh of local gates is trained step by step, nulling response blocks until the total transformation reaches identity.
layout: 2 stacked panels: circuit diagram on top, 8 heatmaps below, left-to-right
description: Panel (a) shows a four-mode photonic circuit drawn as horizontal wires from In 4 to In 1. A large gray box labeled S_unk sits on the left. To its right is a triangular mesh of colored two-mode gate boxes labeled S, with L1 to L4 tags and red step numbers 1 to 6. Orange, pink and cyan boxes mark successive layers, and four green single-mode gates share step 7. Small × and ✓ marks at each gate's ports show which outputs are nulled. Port labels are color-coded and a legend sits below. Panel (b) is a row of eight viridis heatmaps of |S_θ S_unk|, one per training step. Red boxes mark the block being nulled in each step. The matrices go from dense and noisy to block diagonal, then to a bright diagonal identity. Axes are labeled with input probe and output port.
caption: (a) Symplectic Reck mesh for $N=4$ modes. Red step numbers show the gate training order. The final single-mode gates can be trained in parallel. (b) Simulated response $|S_\theta S_{\rm unk}|$ during the training steps. Red boxes mark the blocks being nulled and correspond to the step numbers in (a). Two-mode gates bring the response close to block diagonal, and single-mode gates bring it close to the identity, with a final residual of $1.1\times10^{-4}$. Each panel uses its own color scale.
abstract: Programmable photonic circuits are a natural platform for physical learning, where hardware parameters are trained directly from measured feedback. We propose a physical learning algorithm and architecture for continuous-variable quantum systems where a photonic circuit is trained in situ to invert an unknown lossless Gaussian quantum operation. We prove that a generic symplectic matrix $S\in\mathrm{Sp}(2N,\mathbb{R})$ admits a decomposition into a triangular array of two-mode symplectic gates on neighboring modes, followed by single-mode symplectic gates. We then introduce the symplectic Reck mesh, which physically realizes this factorization, generalizing the unitary Reck mesh widely used in optical neural networks. When placed after an unknown Gaussian unitary, the mesh is trained in situ by nulling local response blocks one at a time using optical probes and measurements. We identify a local condition number that quantifies the squeezing required for a nulling step and its sensitivity to measurement error. We numerically demonstrate finite-shot training and robustness to systematic gate-calibration errors. Our work extends self-configuring optical networks from unitary to symplectic transformations, bringing physical learning to continuous-variable quantum photonic hardware.
